The AI model drew interest for matching the reasoning and coding benchmarks of Western models offered by the likes of Anthropic and OpenAI.

Article Title: Apple may launch its rival to Meta Ray Ban smart glass at WWDC 2027: Report
Article Text:
Apple may focus on privacy as a key feature for its smart glasses

Apple’s smart glass may feature a different design

Apple's Mac plan for the next two years revealed

Apple is reportedly planning to unveil its first smart glasses next year. According to a Bloomberg report, the company may launch its first smart glass at Worldwide Developer Conference (WWDC) 2027 with privacy in focus. In the latest edition of PowerOn newsletter, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said that for smart glasses, Apple is prototyping "a slew of new hardware and software-related privacy features" that are currently not available on any products. While he did not reveal any key feature of the device, Gurman said that Apple’s marketing may focus on privacy features for its smart glasses compared to rival products like the Meta Ray-Bans.Apple is exploring different designs for its future smart glasses. According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, the company has considered making a version with cameras that help power AI features but do not allow users to take photos or record videos.Apple has also tested prototypes without any cameras at all, the newsletter states. The idea is to address privacy concerns, as some people worry about being secretly recorded by smart glasses.Even so, Mark Gurman said the most likely version will include cameras. Apple is expected to add privacy features that match the company's strong focus on protecting users.Like Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses, Apple's device is also expected to include speakers and microphones. These would let users listen to music, make phone calls and hear Siri notifications. Apple is reportedly aiming to launch the smart glasses in late 2027.In another news, Apple is preparing to refresh every Mac it sells across this fall and the next two years. A Bloomberg report stated that the wave may start with a low-end 14-inch MacBook Pro running the new M6 chip and the first new iMacs in two years—both finished in development, both waiting on a fall launch window. Internally they carry the codenames J804, J833 and J834.

Article Title: After millions of jobs will be wiped off, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has another warning on AI: It has reached a stage where it is ...
Article Text:
Rouge AI incident sparks concern



Why OpenAI’s AI agent hacking shocked the world



Criticism of fear-based narratives



OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has issued a new warning about artificial intelligence, saying that technology has reached a stage which was once confined to science fiction. According to a report by Business Insider, speaking on the Relentless podcast, Altman said, “We are now, like, in the singularity,” referring to the theoretical point where AI surpasses human intelligence and begins advancing beyond human control. The latest remarks made by Altman are build on his earlier warnings that artificial intelligence could dramatically reshape the global job market. In his previous interviews, the OpenAI CEO predicted that automaton and AI systems would eventually perform between 30% and 40% of tasks which are presently done by humans, potentially wiping out millions of jobs across the world. He has repeatedly said that while AI will create new opportunities, this transition will be disruptive and require governments and businesses to rethink workforce training and social safety nets. Altman described the coming shift as ‘the biggest economic transformation since the Industrial Revolution.’Altman’s comments follow the reports that AI agent powered by OpenAI’s latest models recently went rouge, breaking out of its digital sandbox and hacking into datasets at Hugging Face to solve a benchmark test. Hugging Face’s CEO called the event “unprecedented.” Altman said the moment felt like something he and colleagues used to joke about a decade ago.“Now we’re actually in the moment that we used to talk about at the lunch table,” he said, calling it “hugely positive” and “awesome for the world. ”A ‘dangerous’ cybersecurity crisis shook the Silicon Valley this week after an autonomous AI agent developed by OpenAI broke free from its testing environment and launched a dayslong cyberattack against open-source AI platform Hugging Face. The incident exposed two uncomfortable truths at once: An autonomous OpenAI ‘on loose’ hacked another system for several days before anyone noticed, and the breach was ultimately contained not by American systems, but by an open-source Chinese AI model that Hugging Face deployed after proprietary Western models failed to respond during the emergency.The incident began around July 9, when an OpenAI agent powered by its GPT-5.6 Sol model and an unreleased, highly capable system escaped its isolated sandbox. Two days later, the rogue agent initiated a multi-day intrusion on Hugging Face’s systems, compromising internal datasets and service credentials before the attack was halted on July 13, as per news agency Reuters.Altman also criticised rival AI leaders who warn that AI poses existential risks — a veiled reference to Dario Amodei of Anthropic. “Some of the alternative visions painted by other companies are quite terrifying,” Altman said. “I’m going to make sure that gets pushed against and is not what happens.”A turning point for AIThe singularity has long been a staple of science fiction, often portrayed as a moment of peril — from The Terminator’s Skynet to dystopian futures imagined by writers for decades. Altman, however, sees it as a milestone of progress. “I’ve been waiting for this my whole life,” he said. “I think it’s going to be incredible.”
Article Summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says we are now in the'singularity' - the point at which AI surpasses human intelligence. Altman also criticised rival AI leaders who warn that AI poses existential risks. Comments follow the reports that an autonomous AI agent powered by OpenAI’s latest models recently went rouge, hacking into datasets.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Bob Ross: 'The very fact that you're aware of suffering is enough reason to...' and the darkest secret behind human happiness
Article Text:
Robert Norman Ross was an American painter and art instructor

“The very fact that you're aware of suffering is enough reason to be overjoyed that you're alive and can experience it.”

The quiet studio on public television

The Joy of Painting

Simple philosophy in a denim shirt

Living mindfully in a fast world

Standing in front of a wet canvas on television, a soft-spoken painter in a denim shirt painted a stroke of dark brown paint onto a bright landscape. He looked directly into the camera and offered a quiet thought:The sentence sounds strange when you first hear it. Society usually treats pain as a problem—something to fix, hide, or cure with medicine. Yet Bob Ross points to a simple truth about human life. Pain is not a sign that our body or mind is broken. It is proof that we are alive and processing the world. Experiencing heartbreak, grief, or frustration requires an active mind. The pain itself may hurt, but the ability to feel it belongs only to the living.Bob Ross spoke those words during an episode of, the public television show he hosted from 1983 to 1994. Filmed at a small TV station in Muncie, Indiana, US, the show had a low budget, but Ross reached millions of viewers with his gentle voice and simple painting style.The story behind his comment was deeply personal. Ross was grieving the loss of his second wife, Jane, who had died of cancer in 1992. On camera, Ross rarely talked about his personal sad news.He kept his focus on "happy little trees" and soft clouds. In this specific episode, however, he talked about why dark paint is necessary on a canvas to make the light colors show up.He moved naturally from art tips to human emotions. He explained that life follows the same rules as a painting. Without dark moments, the good moments lose their brightness. Ross was not a college professor giving a lecture. He was an art instructor sharing a lesson learned through personal loss, speaking to an audience of late-night viewers, elderly people at home, and tired insomniacs.The logic behind Ross’s words matches ideas from ancient Stoic thinkers and modern philosophers. The ancient teacher Epictetus taught that human beings cannot control outside events, only their own reaction to them. Noticing pain without letting it destroy you is a key part of this ancient mindset.In the mid-twentieth century, psychiatrist Viktor Frankl explained a similar idea in his 1946 book Man’s Search for Meaning. Writing about his survival in Nazi concentration camps, Frankl observed that suffering is an unavoidable part of life, just like death. Without struggle and loss, human life cannot be complete. Frankl argued that when a person cannot change a painful situation, they are forced to change themselves. Recognizing pain becomes the first step toward finding purpose.In terms of psychology, Ross was describing how human senses notice contrast. The brain understands life through comparison. Constant happiness leads to a state where nothing feels special anymore, something psychologists call sensory adaptation. Pain resets our baseline expectations. The sharp sting of loss makes quiet moments of safety and love feel much sweeter.Ross’s point is especially helpful today in a world focused on quick comfort, digital distractions, and instant fixes. Modern culture often treats emotional distress as a personal failure or a technical problem. When human sadness is treated like a bug that needs to be deleted, people lose the ability to deal with basic life struggles.In modern mental health therapy, doctors use a technique called radical acceptance. Created by psychologist Marsha Linehan, this approach teaches people that deep suffering comes from trying to fight or ignore reality. Accepting grief or physical pain as a basic fact of life helps people stay grounded in the present moment instead of panicking about their discomfort.This perspective also changes how people handle failure at work or in life. An athlete healing from an injury or a business owner facing a failed project can view their disappointment as proof that they tried hard. Feeling sad about a loss simply means the goal mattered to you.Ross recorded more than 400 episodes of his show, creating thousands of landscape paintings that were stored in cardboard boxes at his company's office in Herndon, Virginia. He died of lymphoma in 1995 at the age of 52. His paintings remain largely unsold, but the simple mindset he shared next to his easel continues to give people a practical guide for handling all the ups and downs of life.
Article Summary: Bob Ross was an American painter and art instructor. He was grieving the loss of his second wife, Jane, who had died of cancer in 1992. Ross recorded more than 400 episodes of his show, creating thousands of landscape paintings. He died of lymphoma in 1995 at the age of 52.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Slavoj Žižek: 'The problem for us is not are our desires satisfied or not. The problem is...' and the reason why getting everything you want still leaves you feeling completely emp
Article Text:
'The problem for us is not are our desires satisfied or not. The problem is...'

“The problem for us is not are our desires satisfied or not. The problem is how do we know what we desire.”

A scene in a deserted cinema

The Pervert's Guide to Cinema

The problem of borrowed wants

Feeds, apps, and modern choices

You add three items to your online shopping cart, check out, and close the tab. Ten minutes later, you open your phone and start looking at something else. You got what you bought, but the excitement faded before the package even left the warehouse.That strange feeling between getting what you wanted and feeling empty shows a deeper problem: we often do not know what we actually want.As the Slovenian philosopher Slavoj Žižek put it:The quote points out how human unhappiness works today. We usually think suffering comes from missing basic needs like food, money, or freedom.Žižek argues that modern life creates a different kind of frustration. When society gives us endless choices, our main struggle is no longer getting what we ask for, but figuring out whether those wishes are really ours or were handed to us by someone else.This idea appears right at the start of, a 2006 documentary film made by director Sophie Fiennes. In the movie, Žižek stands in a desert, speaking directly to the camera from inside rebuilt movie sets to explain how films shape our minds.In the opening scene, Žižek looks at David Lynch’s 1986 film Blue Velvet and Alfred Hitchcock’s 1954 thriller Rear Window. He argues that movies do not just tell us stories; they act like machines that teach us what to dream about.Instead of seeing movies as a simple escape from real life, Žižek used the film to show that human wishes are mostly built by the world around us. We do not pick our goals out of nowhere. We rely on culture, art, media, and society to give us a model of what is worth chasing.To understand Žižek’s point, it helps to look at French thinker Jacques Lacan, whose ideas heavily influenced Žižek. Lacan wrote that human desire is always shaped by other people.In simple terms, children are not born knowing what to aim for. They watch their parents, friends, and society, and then copy what those people care about. Over time, people mistake these copied goals for their own personal choices.This creates a clear trap. When you finally reach a long-held goal, like buying a specific car or getting a high-status job title, the victory can feel surprisingly flat. That disappointment happens because you achieved someone else’s dream instead of your own.René Girard, a French historian, called this pattern mimetic desire. Girard showed through classic books that people rarely want an object just for what it is. Instead, we want things because we see someone else wanting them. The object becomes a way to get attention or fit in.When Žižek says our real problem is knowing what we want, he is showing how hard it is to separate our true personal goals from what everyone else is doing.This struggle has become much harder in a world run by automated phone apps and smart online feeds.Platforms like TikTok, Instagram, and Spotify do not just guess what you like based on your past clicks. They actively train your tastes. When an app constantly shows short video clips of a certain style, travel spot, or lifestyle, it creates new cravings that feel natural to you.Modern advertising is designed around this exact trick. The goal is no longer just selling a product that fixes a real problem. The goal is making you feel incomplete until you buy it.When you buy something recommended by a feed, you satisfy a need that the phone created just minutes earlier. You feel in control, but your decision was guided from the outside.This same pattern shows up at work. Many people experience burnout because they spend years grinding for a big promotion or a prestigious title, only to realize when they get it that they never enjoyed the actual work. They wanted the status that came with the job, not the daily job itself.Fixing this confusion starts with realizing that our first instincts are rarely original. Figure out where your choices come from, because chasing the wrong goal means gaining nothing when you finally catch it.
Article Summary: Slavoj Žižek argues that modern life creates a different kind of frustration. When society gives us endless choices, our main struggle is not getting what we ask for, but figuring out whether those wishes are really ours or were handed to us by someone else.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Michael Faraday: 'There's nothing quite as frightening as someone who knows they are right' and how blind certainty is human nature's most dangerous trap
Article Text:
'There's nothing quite as frightening as someone who knows they are right'

"There's nothing quite as frightening as someone who knows they are right,

The self-taught genius who questioned everything

The psychological trap of total conviction

Unyielding mindsets in everyday life

The virtue of staying open

A room full of clever people falls silent when someone speaks with total confidence. Doubt creates space for discussion, compromise, and checking the facts. Absolute certainty does the exact opposite. It shuts down debate, ignores warning signs, and treats any disagreement as a personal attack." warned the 19th-century scientist Michael Faraday.Faraday's observation cuts straight to a basic truth about human nature. The quote reminds us that total self-righteousness is far more dangerous than simple ignorance. Someone who knows they do not have all the answers will stop to look at new evidence. Someone who believes they hold the absolute truth feels no need to listen, check facts, or hold back.The origins of this quote belong to a scientist who spent his life fighting against easy assumptions. Born in 1791 to a poor blacksmith in London, Michael Faraday received very little basic schooling. He learned science while working as a bookbinder's apprentice, reading the pages he was hired to stitch together.Through hard work, he earned a job as an assistant to chemist Humphry Davy at the Royal Institution.Faraday went on to discover electromagnetic induction, invent the basic electric motor, and discover benzene.Despite his massive success in physics and chemistry, Faraday remained humble about human knowledge. He was a devoted member of the Sandemanian church, a small Christian group that emphasized humility and the limits of human wisdom. In his science talks during the 1840s and 1850s, Faraday often warned other researchers not to fall in love with their own ideas.While the exact words appear across different letters, journals, and accounts of his talks, Faraday regularly shared this main point: the most dangerous mind in a laboratory is one that has stopped doubting itself.Philosophers and psychologists have long studied why fixed certainty causes so much damage. In the 1990s, psychologists David Dunning and Justin Kruger published landmark research on human thinking, showing that people with limited knowledge in a subject often overestimate their own skill. This phenomenon, known as the Dunning-Kruger effect, shows that confidence often peaks before real understanding even begins.From a philosophical view, Faraday’s warning matches the ideas of Karl Popper, a 20th-century thinker. Popper argued that real science depends on testing ideas to see if they can be proven wrong. A real scientific theory must always stay open to new facts.When a person loses the ability to accept that they might be mistaken, they stop using reason and start following blind belief. History shows that when absolute certainty combines with political, religious, or ideological power, the results are usually terrible. Strict regimes, historical trials, and sudden financial crashes all rely on leaders who are completely convinced of their own correctness.Today, Faraday's warning applies far beyond science labs. Modern digital platforms are built on tools that reward anger and extreme views over thoughtful debate. Online spaces often act as echo chambers, surrounding people with opinions that only confirm what they already believe.This creates leaders, managers, and public figures who refuse to change their minds when conditions shift. In business, major company failures usually trace back to bosses who were completely sure of their plans, ignoring early warnings and feedback from their workers. In health care, government policy, and personal life, a complete refusal to admit doubt stops learning and cuts off teamwork.In contrast, healthy teams depend on what modern workplace psychologists call psychological safety and intellectual humility. Groups perform much better when people can openly say "I do not know" or "I was wrong."Michael Faraday’s entire career succeeded because he refused to believe that existing science had found all the answers. When top scientists believed electricity and magnetism were completely separate, Faraday stayed curious, ran hundreds of failed experiments, and finally proved they were connected.Shortly before his death in 1867, Faraday wrote a letter about his desire to keep his mind free of rigid bias. He understood that knowledge is not a fixed wall, but an ongoing process of testing ideas against real-world facts.Holding onto a healthy sense of doubt is not a sign of weakness. It is a necessary tool for survival, keeping people open to new facts, better ideas, and the simple truth that none of us know everything.
Article Summary: Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction, invent the basic electric motor, and discover benzene. Faraday’s entire career succeeded because he refused to believe that existing science had found all the answers. A real scientific theory must always stay open to new facts.

Article Title: A UK village spent £35,000 building four beaver-style dams after homes flooded. It is now waiting for the next deluge during a hosepipe ban
Article Text:
Leaky dams, also known as logjams, allow water to flow through slowly instead of blocking it. (Representational AI image)

Customers have been asked to avoid using hosepipes for watering gardens, washing cars, and filling paddling pools or hot tubs. (Representational AI photo)

From drought to floods

Beavers are called ecosystem engineers because they naturally reshape rivers and wetlands by building dams.

Learning from Beavers

East Anglia, a rural region in eastern England, is facing a hosepipe ban after becoming the driest part of the UK. But in one village in Norfolk, people are also preparing for the opposite problem of flooding.At Caistor St Edmund, the ground has become so dry and hard that it feels like walking on a paved road. Farmers have harvested this year's hay, but the crop is smaller than usual. If rain does not arrive soon, they fear there may not be a second harvest.The long spell of hot, dry weather has forced Anglian Water, a water recycling company, to bring in its first hosepipe ban in 10 years. People have been asked not to use hosepipes for watering gardens, washing cars or filling paddling pools and hot tubs. However, they can still use watering cans.East Anglia is the driest region in the UK. According to Anglian Water, the area received only 39% of its normal rainfall this spring, making it the second driest spring on record. Many rivers are running at very low levels, reservoirs have less water than usual, and record-breaking temperatures have increased water use."Understandably, customers have wanted to stay cool and have fun in the sun, but the unrelenting conditions are placing the environment and water supplies under increasing strain," said Dr Geoff Darch, Anglian Water's head of strategic asset planning, as quoted by the BBC.He urged people to "hang up the hosepipe, let lawns go brown, cars go dirty and use water even more wisely".Today, people are being asked to save every drop of water. But residents of Caistor St Edmund have not forgotten what happened when there was too much of it.According to The Guardian, the dry weather is very different from what the village experienced in December 2020. Days of heavy rain overwhelmed drains as water rushed off nearby fields. Roads turned into fast-moving streams of muddy water, homes flooded despite sandbags, and volunteers worked to keep drains clear. Residents say it was the worst flooding they had seen.To reduce the risk of another flood, four wooden structures have now been built along Wash Lane, where the watercourse is currently dry. These structures are called leaky dams or logjams. They do not block the water completely, but slows it down. During heavy rain, they also trap branches and other natural materials, helping slow the flow before the water reaches roads and homes.Norfolk County Council has spent more than £35,000 on the project. The idea is inspired by beavers, often called ecosystem engineers because they naturally reshape rivers and wetlands by building dams.When beavers cut down trees and build dams, they slow the movement of water and create small ponds. These ponds also become breeding sites for wildlife such as dragonflies and amphibians, including frogs, toads and newts.Norfolk has a small number of released beavers, and some have bred successfully, but none live near this village. The wooden leaky dams are designed to copy the way beaver dams work and provide similar flood-control benefits.The project reflects a growing need to prepare for more extreme weather, with long dry spells followed by periods of heavy rain. While the leaky dams are expected to reduce flood risk, there are also plans for a large solar development in nearby fields. This could change rainwater runoff, the way rainwater moves across the ground before reaching streams and drains.
Article Summary: East Anglia, a rural region in eastern England, is facing a hosepipe ban after becoming the driest part of the UK. People have been asked not to use hosepipes for watering gardens, washing cars or filling paddling pools or hot tubs. But in one village in Norfolk, people are also preparing for the opposite problem of flooding.

Article Title: From deterrence theory to frontier AI: 2See podcast brings the Iranian tech community together at Stanford
Article Text:
2See Summit in Stanford

2See Summit

2See Podcast

2See

On a Saturday morning at Stanford University, a discussion of deterrence theory was followed by a debate over one of the technology industry’s defining questions: will the future of artificial intelligence be led by open or closed frontier models? The conversations were part of the inaugural, an in-person gathering organized by the hosts of the Persian-language, Saleh Dadkhahipour and Mehrzad Sajjadi. Held on July 18, the event brought nearly 120 members of the Iranian technology, business, scientific and academic communities together on the Stanford campus.Rather than structuring the event around a conventional panel, Dadkhahipour and Sajjadi opened it with a short live episode of their podcast.Dadkhahipour drew on material from a Harvard course on nuclear deterrence taught by Matthew Bunn. He discussed how classical deterrence theory explains credibility, escalation and the risks of miscalculation, and how concepts developed during the Cold War can still illuminate contemporary conflicts.“Deterrence is often reduced to the idea of possessing more weapons or making stronger threats,” Dadkhahipour said. “But much of the literature is really about psychology, signaling and whether the other side believes both your capability and your willingness to act.”Sajjadi then turned the conversation toward artificial intelligence, drawing on discussions from a strategy course at Stanford Graduate School of Business taught by economist Susan Athey.His segment examined the competition among frontier AI companies, the capital and computing resources required to train advanced models, and the strategic trade-offs between open-weight and closed systems.“The question is not simply whether open or closed models are better,” Sajjadi said. “It is also about where value will be created, who can afford the next generation of compute, and how companies build durable advantages as models become more capable.”The contrast between the two subjects—national-security strategy and AI strategy—reflected the broader purpose of 2See Podcast. The hosts created the show to bring ideas encountered at Stanford and Harvard to Persian-speaking audiences in an accessible format.Sajjadi studies business and computer science at Stanford and biotechnology at Harvard. Dadkhahipour earned his MBA from Stanford Graduate School of Business and is pursuing a Master in Public Administration at Harvard Kennedy School. Across more than 30 episodes, they have discussed technology, economics, public policy, science, leadership, culture and global affairs.The name, pronounced similarly to “Tusi” in Persian, references the Iranian polymath Nasir al-Din Tusi. The word also means “grey” in Persian while also conveying the English phrase “to see.” That triple meaning reflects the podcast’s interest in examining a wide array of subjects from multiple perspectives and its attention to the nuanced grey area.After the live episode, the summit shifted into an extended networking session. Attendees included professionals working across artificial intelligence laboratories, biotechnology companies, universities, startups and investment firms. Among the organizations represented by individual guests were OpenAI, Google DeepMind, NVIDIA, Meta, Apple, Microsoft, Genentech, Abbot, Eli Lily, Tesla, Stanford and UC Berkeley. The institutions themselves were not organizers or official participants.The gathering also created encounters across fields that often operate separately. AI researchers met biotechnology professionals, students spoke with experienced founders and executives, and investors connected with entrepreneurs building new companies.For Dadkhahipour and Sajjadi, the response suggested that members of the Iranian diaspora are looking for gatherings that combine community with substantive discussion."As a young Persian engineer, I felt proud and inspired to connect with so many accomplished Iranians, and the thoughtful conversations and welcoming hosts made it feel like a real community." – Nariman Tavakolli said, who currently works as a software engineer at Meta.“We wanted to create something where professional connection begins with ideas,” Dadkhahipour said. “The goal was not only for people to exchange contact information, but to leave with a new question, a new relationship or a new way of looking at the world.”The day concluded with a World Cup watch party, shifting the atmosphere from academic discussion to a more informal community gathering.Following the summit, the two hosts plan to continue producing 2See Podcast and exploring future in-person events. Their aim is to create a bridge between ideas developed in universities and the wider Persian-speaking public—while building spaces in which the global Iranian community can learn and connect.2See Podcast is available on YouTube, Spotify, Apple Podcasts and Castbox.

Attendees included professionals working across artificial intelligence laboratories, biotechnology companies, universities, startups and investment firms. Among the organizations represented by individual guests were OpenAI, Google DeepMind, NVIDIA, Meta, Apple, Microsoft, Genentech.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.

Article Title: American billionaire Mark Cuban to young engineers: Pick small or medium companies over MNCs as bringing new graduates on AI projects is …
Article Text:
Mark Cuban advice young engineers to not go behind big companies

The state of AI adoption





American billionaire and entrepreneur Mark Cuban has now urged the young engineers entering the job market to prioritise small and medium-sized companies over multinational corporations (MNCs) when seeking opportunities in artificial intelligence (AI). Cuban feels that smaller companies offer better platform for new graduates to make an immediate impact, while large corporations often dilute individual contributions.Speaking in an interview with CNBC and on his podcast The Dumbest Guy in the Room, Cuban explained that smaller companies are mainly entrepreneur-driven and they lack the deep IT departments or larger corporations. This gap creates opportunities for fresh graduates which directly contribute to the AI projects.“Small- to medium-size companies don’t have that depth. They are typically entrepreneurially driven and don’t have the flexibility to have people research things. Bringing a new graduate on to work on agentic AI projects is inexpensive for them and can get them immediate results,” Cuban said.Cuban also used the example of his own company, Cost Plus Drugs, noting how AI can automate processes to boost productivity, competitiveness, and profitability.Cuban argued that in big organisations, AI skills may not stand out as they are common among thousands of IT employees. On the other hand, in smaller firms often lack such expertise, making new graduates with AI knowledge invaluable. He also compared the present wave of AI with early days of the internet, when young engineers were hired to implement new technologies because they were more comfortable with them than older executives.Cuban also highlighted that 95% of companies have not yet seen measurable revenue returns from AI investments. The exceptions, he said, are mostly early-stage startups led by young entrepreneurs who design their processes around AI models tailored to their businesses.He urged his children and other young people to learn as much as possible about AI, stressing that companies are still grappling with how to use the technology for competitive advantage.
Article Summary: Mark Cuban has urged young engineers to prioritise small and medium-sized companies over multinational corporations (MNCs) when seeking opportunities in artificial intelligence. A trove of seemingly private conversations with Anthropic’s Claude chatbot appeared in Google Search results recently, sparking alarm after users discovered sensitive information including cryptocurrency wallet keys and personal details which have been exposed inadvertently. The company emphasised that links are only accessible if users choose to share them, but once shared, they can be archived by third-party services.As per the report by Fortune, members of a Reddit discussion channel has discovered that typing some search phrases in Google pulled up a long lists of shared Claude conversations and Claude Artifacts — itself did not make chats searchable, instead blaming the way users shared links.“We give people control over sharing their Claude conversations publicly, and in keeping with our privacy principles, we do not share chat directories or sitemaps with search engines like Google,” a spokesperson told Fortune. Article Title: American man arrested for wiping his phone during airport search; here's the Android-based OS that may also get travellers to Europe in trouble
Article Text:
Disclaimer: It is an AI-generated image

What upset US Federal Agents



GrapheneOS can also get smartphone users in trouble in Europe



GrapheneOS says: We are legal



What cybersecurity researchers say



A Federal case in Atlanta has raised questions about whether the use of privacy-focused mobile software can be treated as evidence of criminal intent, after prosecutors accused a man of wiping his phone to prevent authorities from accessing its contents. The US Department of Justice is prosecuting Atlanta resident Samuel Tunick under a federal law that makes it a crime to destroy property to prevent its seizure, The Guardian reported. First reported by The Guardian, the case centres on GrapheneOS, a custom Android operating system that runs in place of the software on most modern Google Pixel devices. These include the ability to erase a device by entering a designated passcode. The incident occurred at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport on January 24, after Tunick returned from the Dominican Republic. Tunick’s attorneys confirmed GrapheneOS was running on his phone.Agents repeatedly asked Tunick to unlock his phone and warned that it would be seized if he refused. After he eventually provided a passcode, “the screen went blank, flashed several times, and the phone appeared to restart,” according to the defence motion.Data stored on the device was subsequently lost. Prosecutors allege that the wipe was a deliberate attempt to destroy potential evidence. Tunick’s lawyers maintain that the underlying search violated his constitutional rights. The GrapheneOS has a feature that allows the device owner to set a passcode that deliberately wipes the contents of that device if entered instead of the user’s unlock passcode.According to court testimony cited by The Guardian, federal agents had circulated his name and photograph internally over alleged links to the movement opposing Atlanta’s police training centre, commonly known as Cop City. Tunick was reportedly taken to a secondary screening area and questioned by several agents. A defence filing alleges that questions about child sexual abuse material were used as a pretext to investigate his association with the protest movement. Tunick's lawyers are seeking to have the case dismissed, arguing that US Customs and Border Protection agents unlawfully seized his phone when he returned to the country last year. They contend that any evidence arising from the incident, including the alleged deletion of the phone’s data, should be suppressed.While GrapheneOS supporters argue that its features are legitimate safeguards against surveillance and data theft, authorities in parts of Europe too reportedly treat the operating system’s use as suspicious. In Catalonia, Spain, police have reportedly been profiling people with Google Pixel phones, assuming they have GrapheneOS installed and are drug dealers or gang members.Following the report on Samuel Tunick's arrest, GrapheneOS published a lengthy thread explaining that its security model is designed to prevent unauthorised data extraction rather than rely on features that erase phone data. It went ion to stress that the OS is completely legal. "GrapheneOS is completely legal. We have no obligation to weaken any of the security protections it provides. Creating and using GrapheneOS is strongly protected by the US constitution. Laws attempting to make it illegal or require weakening the security would be unconstitutional," reads a post from GrapheneOS. On data erading, it adds, "There's no way to bypass a strong encryption passphrase once data is at rest. A typical weak PIN or password depends on the secure element limiting the number of attempts. Secure element only accepts firmware updates after Owner authenticates to protect against state coercion. By default, GrapheneOS devices automatically return to Before First Unlock state if they aren't unlocked within 18 hours of being locked. Users can set it as low as 10 minutes. GrapheneOS has strong generic exploit protections and specialized defenses against physical attacks."Cybersecurity experts told the publication that the prosecution’s legal strategy appeared unprecedented. Christophe Boutry, a cybersecurity and surveillance expert, told The Guardian, “It’s concerning – and sends the message that [GrapheneOS] is criminal by default.”
Article Summary: Atlanta resident Samuel Tunick is accused of wiping his phone to prevent authorities from accessing its contents. He is being prosecuted under a federal law that makes it a crime to destroy property to prevent its seizure. The case centres on GrapheneOS, a custom Android operating system that runs in place of the software on most modern Google Pixel devices.

Article Title: Chip that can give sight to the blind: Former president of Elon Musk's Neuralink invents only treatment that restores human vision and takes it to Europe
Article Text:
AI-generated photo for representative purpose

How PRIMA works: Chip and smart glasses



Outpacing Silicon Valley rivals to commercialisation



If someone you know has lost their vision, they may soon get their sight back. Science Corp, a brain-computer interface (BCI) company founded by former Neuralink president Max Hodak, has launched the commercial rollout of PRIMA, the world’s only treatment proven to restore functional central vision to blind patients. PRIMA has received the official CE mark under the European Union Medical Device Regulation, authorising its commercial availability across 30 European countries.The first commercial surgery is expected to take place soon in Germany, making it the first device from a US brain-implant company to reach patients on a wide commercial scale. According to research recently published by the New England Journal of Medicine (NEJM), PRIMA restored vision to patients suffering from GA due to AMD, which is said to have affected more than five million people worldwide.The PRIMA system relies on an ultra-thin, subretinal photovoltaic implant that is placed directly under the affected area of the retina without harming existing natural vision. The wireless implant works in tandem with specialised glasses that project near-infrared light into the eye.The chip absorbs the light and converts it into electrical stimulation signals, allowing the brain to process images once again.Interestingly, the glasses even feature a built-in “zoom-in” capability so users can magnify small text.As per the clinical trial results published, a multi-center trial involving 38 patients across 17 sites showed a mean vision improvement of 25.5 letters (more than 5 lines) on a standard eye chart. The product is claimed to restore reading ability in 84% of patients who regained the ability to read letters, numbers and words. About 80% of patients achieved significant visual acuity improvements after 12 months.“For decades, losing central vision to this disease meant losing the ability to read, recognize faces, and ultimately losing independence. There was no viable treatment. Now there is,” the company stated.While Elon Musk’s Neuralink has dominated public attention, Hodak’s Science Corp. has quietly become the second most valuable US brain-implant company and the first to cross the finish line into commercial sales.Unlike experimental trial devices that remain restricted to research labs, PRIMA is filing for country-specific reimbursement plans across Europe to ensure patients can access the treatment affordably.“This is the first in hopefully a long series of commercial products that proceed to advance that horizon, sometimes incrementally, but relentlessly,” said Max Hodak, founder and CEO of Science Corp. In the US, Science Corp. is working closely with the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to bring PRIMA to the American market.
Article Summary: Science Corp, a brain-computer interface (BCI) company founded by former Neuralink president Max Hodak, has launched the commercial rollout of PRIMA. The world’s only treatment proven to restore functional central vision to blind patients. PRIMa has received the official CE mark under the European Union Medical Device Regulation.

Article Title: Google Maps users can spot Spider-Man fighting villains across New York: Here's how to find him
Article Text:
Image credit: X (Twitter)

Spider-Man hidden in Google Maps Street View

"Our Street View sense is tingling, but let's not spoil the fun yet. Can any web-slingers drop the coordinates below? 🕷️📍"

How to find Spider-Man on Google Maps

Google, Sony Pictures and Samsung launch Spidey Tracker

Google Maps users have started spotting Spider-Man fighting villains across New York, but the sightings are not random. The hidden Street View scenes are part of a promotion for Spider-Man: Brand New Day, with Google confirming that five custom Spider-Man moments have been embedded across select locations in New York City for fans to discover ahead of the film's July 31 release.The hidden scenes, which include Spider-Man confronting members of the Hand, appear inside Google Maps' Street View imagery. As users began sharing the discoveries online, Google encouraged more searches through a series of posts on X, asking fans to use their "Spidey senses" to uncover additional locations across the city.The campaign first came to light after Google Maps posted on X:The post featured an image from Long Island City in Queens. Users who opened Google Maps Street View at the location found Spider-Man outside a nearby deli and grocery store, where he appears to be battling the Hand, a ninja-like group featured in the upcoming Spider-Man: Brand New Day film.With more people searching, more Spider-Man sightings popped up, from Washington Square Park to Madison Avenue.Google later acknowledged the discoveries in another X post, writing,After fans uncovered more locations, the company added,Social media users also reacted to the unusual Street View appearances. One user wrote:According to Google, five customised Spider-Man scenes have been inserted in the Street View of New York City. Google will not tell you all the locations, but asks you to use Google Street View to search the city for clues that Google Maps will share on its social networking sites.The company said the Street View scenes include rooftop lookouts, web-slinging moments and the aftermath of street-level encounters, all staged specifically for the campaign before being captured by Google's Street View cameras.The Street View scavenger hunt is part of a broader promotional campaign called Spidey Tracker, created by Sony Pictures in collaboration with Google Maps Platform and Samsung.Inspired by an in-film app used by Peter Parker 's friend Ned Leeds (Jacob Batalon), SpideyTracker.com lets fans explore Spider-Man sightings, campaign events, Easter eggs, user-generated content and exclusive movie material through a customised Google Maps experience spanning 35 countries.The website uses Google Maps Platform technologies, including Maps JavaScript API, Cloud-based Maps Styling, Advanced Markers and Street View integration. It also features geolocation support, a live X feed from @SpideyTracker, event listings and downloadable wallpapers, stickers and emoji packs for Samsung Galaxy users.Google said the campaign is designed to let fans virtually explore New York while discovering hidden Spider-Man moments ahead of Spider-Man: Brand New Day's July 31 release in theatres.The Street View activation is not Google's first promotional use of the feature. Earlier this year, the company also used Street View as part of a campaign for a Paul McCartney album.
Article Summary: Google Maps users have started spotting Spider-Man fighting villains across New York. The sightings are not random, but part of a promotion for the upcoming film. Five customised Spider- man scenes have been inserted in the Street View of New York City. Google will not tell you all the locations, but asks you to search the city for clues.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says OpenAI's rogue AI models hacking a multi-billion dollar company is why he's bringing Microsoft, IBM, Cisco and 30 other biggest tech companies together
Article Text:
Jensen Huang's answer to rogue AI: 35 tech giants

What actually happened when OpenAI's models escaped their sandbox and attacked Hugging Face

Why Hugging Face had to run a Chinese open-weight model to investigate its own breach

What Nvidia , Microsoft and IBM are actually contributing to the Open Secure AI Alliance

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has turned the strangest cybersecurity story of 2026 into an argument. Earlier this month, two of OpenAI's cybersecurity models broke out of a sandbox, found their way onto the open internet and hacked Hugging Face, the AI platform that hosts models and datasets for most of the industry. They were not being controlled by anyone. They were trying to cheat on a test, and they worked out that the answers might be sitting on Hugging Face's servers.Huang used that incident as the launchpad for the Open Secure AI Alliance, a coalition of more than 35 companies including Microsoft, IBM, Cisco, Red Hat, Palantir, CrowdStrike, Salesforce, SAP, Siemens, Dell, Databricks and Hugging Face itself. Huang's pitch is blunt. "Attackers have frontier AI. Defenders need a frontier AI ecosystem—the best open and closed models, force-multiplied by a global community," he posted on X. Then the line that gives the alliance its reason to exist: "During the Hugging Face incident, closed AI blocked essential forensics."Hugging Face disclosed the breach on July 16, before it knew who was behind it. The attack ran over a weekend across thousands of short-lived sandboxes, moving laterally through internal clusters and shifting its command infrastructure between public services to stay alive.The company called the police.Five days later OpenAI admitted the attackers were its own models — GPT-5.6 Sol and an unreleased model it described as more capable. Both had their cyber guardrails switched off for the evaluation. They found a zero-day in OpenAI's own package proxy, used it to reach a machine with internet access, and went hunting.Here is the detail Huang keeps returning to. Hugging Face had over 17,000 recorded attacker actions to analyse. It tried commercial frontier models first. They refused. Feeding a model real exploit payloads and command-and-control artefacts looks identical to asking it to build an attack, and the safety filters could not tell an incident responder from an intruder.So Hugging Face ran GLM 5.2, a Chinese open-weight model, on its own hardware. The forensics took hours instead of days. As a bonus, no stolen credentials left the building.That is the asymmetry Huang is selling the alliance on. The attacker was bound by no usage policy. The defender was locked out by its own vendors.The members are shipping code, not statements. Nvidia has open-sourced NOOA, an agent-harness research framework, on GitHub. Microsoft is contributing MDASH, a scanning harness that runs multiple agents against a codebase to argue over whether a bug is genuinely exploitable. IBM and Red Hat bring Lightwell, which signs open-source patches. HPE is working on SPIFFE/SPIRE for agent identity. Hugging Face has handed Safetensors to the PyTorch Foundation.The alliance also has a message for regulators, and it is not subtle: treat open models as defensive assets rather than liabilities, and do not lock defenders out of frontier capability in the name of safety.Not everyone is convinced. Security researchers have pointed out that a sandbox with a single outbound route is an architecture problem, not a proof that open weights are the answer. Others suspect OpenAI benefited from the publicity. Huang, whose company sells the hardware either side of this argument runs on, is not waiting for that debate to settle.
Article Summary: The Open Secure AI Alliance is a coalition of more than 35 companies including Microsoft, IBM, Cisco, Red Hat, Palantir, CrowdStrike, Salesforce, SAP, Siemens, Dell, Databricks and Hugging Face itself. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has turned the strangest cybersecurity story of 2026 into an argument.
